## Answer

**ITC granted far more equity awards than Tata Motors in FY25 — roughly 4 to 5 times more.**

**ITC – Stock Options:**
During FY25, the eligible employees and Directors of the Company were granted 14,80,700 Stock Options at 'market price' as defined under the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Share Based Employee Benefits and Sweat Equity) Regulations, 2021. This is confirmed in the ESOS movement table, which shows Options granted during the year: – 14,80,700 under the ITC Employee Stock Option Scheme – 2010 (no fresh grants under the older 2006 scheme).

**Tata Motors – PSUs:**
Tata Motors runs two share-based schemes granting PSUs — the TML SLTI Scheme 2021 and the newer TML SLTI Scheme 2024. In FY25, under the TML SLTI Scheme 2021, there were no additional grants of PSUs/Options; all activity that year (vesting/exercise/lapses) related to prior grants. Fresh grants happened only under the newer scheme: In FY25, the Company has granted 3,59,899 PSUs (including superlative PSUs) [under the TML SLTI Scheme 2024]. No PSUs were vested under the TML SLTI Scheme 2024 and no shares were exercised by the employees during the year.

(The financial-statement note on the 2024 scheme records a slightly narrower base-tranche figure of Granted during the year 299,918 PSUs, excluding the "superlative" top-up tranche captured in the governance disclosure above.)

**Comparison:**
- ITC: 14,80,700 stock options granted
- Tata Motors: ~3,59,899 PSUs granted (or ~2,99,918 on the narrower base-grant count)

Using the more complete Tata Motors figure (3,59,899, including superlative PSUs), ITC granted roughly **4.1 times** as many stock options as Tata Motors granted PSUs in FY25. If only the base-tranche count (2,99,918) is used, the multiple rises to roughly **4.9 times**. Either way, ITC's stock-option grants were about **4–5x larger** in number than Tata Motors' PSU grants for FY25.

## Tata Motors' Claim for CY24

In its FY25 annual report, Tata Motors states that the Tata Punch emerged as the #1 car in India in CY24, a claim repeated elsewhere in the report where it notes the strong demand for the Tata Punch, which became the highest‐selling model in the industry in CY24. The report's Integrated Report summary section also flags Punch explicitly as the #1 Model in 2024.

## Best Seller in India So Far in 2026

This falls outside the FY25 annual reports, so I searched current market data. The picture is actually mixed depending on the timeframe you look at:

- **For the full fiscal year FY2026 (April 2025–March 2026)** and into early 2026, the **Maruti Suzuki Dzire** held the top spot — it "was the best-selling car in India for the full FY2026 (April 2025 to March 2026), and it kept that lead going into May 2026."
- **Month-to-month in calendar 2026, the lead has swung back and forth.** In February 2026, the Tata Nexon topped the charts. In June 2026, the Tata Punch took the crown with 21,006 units, "followed by Tata Nexon and Maruti Suzuki Dzire." By July 2026, the Dzire reclaimed the top spot with 23,791 units sold.
- **Looking at the year-to-date (YTD) cumulative ranking through August 2026**, Maruti still leads overall as a brand, but Tata's Punch and Nexon have been gaining fast — "Still, the Tata Punch (+52.7%) and the Tata Nexon (+35%) ranked onto the podium, threatening the leadership of the Maruti Dzire."

**Bottom line:** As of the most recent data (through mid/late 2026), the **Maruti Suzuki Dzire** appears to be India's best-selling car on a cumulative year-to-date basis, though the **Tata Punch** has actually outsold it in individual months (like June 2026) and is closing the gap rapidly — a shift from CY24, when the Punch itself held the annual crown.
